Lighthouse

From the free encyclopedia
Typical lighthouse
PurposeNavigational aid for ships
First builtc. 280 BC

A lighthouse is a tower, building, or other structure designed to emit light to serve as a navigational aid for maritime pilots at sea.[1]

Contents

  • 1 History

History[edit]

Before the development of clearly defined ports, mariners were guided by fires built on hilltops.[2]

An early stone lighthouse on a rocky coast.
